turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Hale, come on back. I'll grab vitals before Dr. Shah sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure, just go easy, bending's the part that gets me. Third-floor walkup, no elevator, and I hauled a couch up those stairs like an idiot.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I told him to wait for the movers. I'm Lauren, his wife. He never listens.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 128 over 82, pulse 76, temperature 36.8 Celsius, oxygen sat 99 percent, and he's breathing 16. You can stay sitting.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 128 okay? Guy at work, Ray, his was like 160-something and he made it sound like he was dying, so now I'm paranoid about those home cuffs.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): 128 over 82 is fine for today. Dr. Shah's finishing a note, she'll be right in.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. Back pain is what I have on the schedule. What's been going on?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Low back. It's a deep ache across the bottom, a little more on the right, about a five or six most of the time. If I lift a case it grabs and jumps to an eight, and I have to stop. Warehouse work is cases of drinks all day, and then we moved, so it's been boxes on boxes.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did it start?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the annoying part. A few weeks, or since the move. And the move, um, I want to say after Halloween, or maybe closer to Thanksgiving, or I'm mixing it up with last year. I really cannot tell you the date.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Don't look at me. I had it as September and then I remembered the lease was later. I can't date it either.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay, so we leave the start date open. Is the pain there every day?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, every day. Stiff in the morning, maybe twenty minutes, then it loosens up. Lying flat on the floor feels better than the new mattress, which was a total ripoff, don't get me started.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Besides lying down, what helps?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen takes the edge off. A hot shower helps a little too. Oh, and the new floor squeaks and the dog loses his mind, totally unrelated, sorry.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's alright. Let me ask the things that would worry me, one at a time. Any numbness or tingling in the legs, feet, or groin?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, my left foot falls asleep if I'm on the forklift too long. That's old, though, for years, and it wakes up when I walk it off. It's not new shooting pins and needles down the leg, and the groin is fine.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): So longstanding foot numbness with sitting, not a new radicular pattern. Next, your bladder. Any trouble starting, leaking, or not knowing when you have to go?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None of that. Peeing is completely normal.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I started telling Lauren I dropped a couple pounds because the kitchen was in boxes and we lived on cereal. There's no scale, though, so I was kinda making up a number.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He did not lose weight. Same jeans, same belt hole. He skipped two lunches and turned it into a documentary.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, she's right. I haven't lost weight.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): So no weight loss. Last one, any fever, chills, or feeling flu-ish?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no chills. I feel well otherwise. The beagle got into the packing paper and I was up late, but that's not sick, that's just a beagle.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any leg weakness, any change in your bowels, or numbness where you sit?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No weakness. Bowels are regular. Nothing numb down there.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. I'm not hearing the dangerous features. How are you actually taking the ibuprofen?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I buy the 200 milligram tablets. I swallow three, so 600 milligrams, two or three times a day on the bad days, not every day. Usually with coffee, which I know isn't food.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any other pain medicine, prescription or somebody else's?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Lauren had tramadol for a tooth. I took one of hers once and I was useless on the forklift, so never again. I'm not taking her pills.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Please don't. Those are mine, and they're almost gone.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Understood. Any allergies to ibuprofen or other medicines?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No drug allergies. Penicillin and ibuprofen are both fine.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any medical problems, surgeries, or family history that matters for the back?

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Surgeries, no. I'm pretty healthy. My dad had a bad back, but he roofed for forty years, so that might just be the job. Oh, and they X-rayed my back once and said it was borderline.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tell me more about that X-ray. What did borderline mean, and when was it?

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Urgent care, I think, or the work clinic, I mix them up. They said borderline, like a little wear, nothing dramatic. Last winter, or the winter before that. I cannot remember which, and they never gave me a number or a report.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I wasn't there. I just remember the word borderline, and he went to work the next day.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): So an old back X-ray called borderline, no report here, and the year is fuzzy. I'll treat that as your recollection, not as a measurement we can use. Let me examine you.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): The muscles on both sides of the low back are tender, the right a little more than the left. The bones in the midline are not tender.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Straight leg raise doesn't send pain down either leg. Strength is full, sensation is intact, and your walk looks normal.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, the pressing is sore right where it grabs. Am I gonna end up with screws like Ray? He still complains, and he also owes me twenty bucks, which is unrelated but it bugs me.

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thinking out loud, this fits mechanical low back pain, a strain from the warehouse lifting and the move. No fever, no bladder change, no new leg findings, and the exam doesn't show a pinched nerve. I can't fully exclude a small disc irritation, but nothing here says surgery.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, good, because I can't take six weeks off. Peak season is coming and my supervisor already side-eyes my bathroom breaks.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bed rest would actually work against you. Stay active, skip the heaviest lifts for now, keep the cases around waist height, and bend your knees. Heat after work is fine.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep the ibuprofen at 600 milligrams by mouth, up to three times a day on bad days, but take it with food instead of just coffee, and skip it when the day is easy. Don't go past that dose.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): With food, got it. Stomach's been fine, no heartburn or anything.
[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll hide the tramadol, and I'll nag him about breakfast. He stands all day too, if that matters.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Standing and lifting both matter. I'm going to refer you to physical therapy for your core and for lifting mechanics. They'll call you to set it up.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): PT, alright. Do I need another X-ray? Last time borderline sounded scary and then nobody did anything.

[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. If it's not better in three weeks, come back and we'll do a lumbar X-ray. Come sooner if you get leg weakness, numbness that sticks around, trouble with your bladder, or a fever.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. What if it just disappears next week? Do I still have to come?
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): No. Only if it's not better. If it settles, cancel. For now I'm calling it mechanical low back pain, provisional, from the story and a reassuring exam.
[SEG0055] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll put it on the calendar as a maybe. And he is not lifting that dryer, I don't care.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright, alright. Thanks. If the beagle asks, the couch won.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): The nurse will have the therapy referral on your way out. Take care of that back.
[SEG0058] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the referral and walk you both out. Watch the step by the desk.
